episode_title: Humans In AI: Kids Ask | What Really Happens Inside a Data Centre?

real_qa.q: How much does it cost to build a data center and how long does construction take?
real_qa.r: Building a data center typically costs 150 to 200 million pounds, with expenses covering the building structure, foundations, and major equipment like generators and batteries. The entire construction process takes about two years from scratch, as equipment orders and delivery times are lengthy and complex.

real_qa.q: Can data centers run on renewable energy sources like solar and wind power?
real_qa.r: Many data centers already use solar and wind power, but the challenge is reliability since data centers must run 24/7/365 and the sun does not shine continuously. Companies like Pure are implementing solutions such as microgrids with biomethane and HVO (vegetable oil) generators, as demonstrated in their Dublin data center.
real_qa.requete: data centers renewable energy solar wind

real_qa.q: What backup systems do data centers have to prevent power outages from shutting them down?
real_qa.r: Data centers have multiple backup options including generators, batteries, and UPS (uninterruptible power supply) systems that activate sequentially if one fails, ensuring they run 24/7/365 as critical national infrastructure without interruption.
real_qa.requete: data center power outage backup systems

real_quote: data centers really is like a hotel for computer servers so those servers sit inside that hotel which is a very secure building
key_stats: 11,000 to 12,000 data centers around the world
150 to 200 million pounds to build a data center
Data center in Harlow uses same water in 20 years as one family of four uses in one year
Vast majority of water used in data centers can be reused
Data centers in UK run 10 to 11 months per year without needing water for cooling
National Data Center Day falls on September 12, the anniversary of data centers becoming critical national infrastructure
